mental_model: One RegBase compilation path turns shape-irregular tensor computation into aligned vector memory IR: normalize shapes first, vectorize into outlined VF callees, merge those callees to a controllable granularity, switch tensor→memref, then mark and realize buffer alignment. Each stage exists because its output is exactly the input representation the next stage needs.
need: A5-class (RegBase) targets need elementwise computation executed as vector instructions over UB buffers whose strides the hardware can align; no single pass can normalize shapes, choose VF granularity, and align memory at once.
purpose: Explain why the six passes coexist as one chain: flattening creates the 1-D form vectorization plans over; AutoVectorizeV2 creates the VF callees MergeVecScope merges; bufferization switches representation; the mark/enable pair delivers aligned memory to lowering.
observable_outcome: Device functions whose elementwise chains run as vector functions over flattened iteration domains, with UB buffers allocated at hardware alignment units behind strided logical views.

audience_contract.who: compiler engineers who know MLIR basics but not the AscendNPU-IR RegBase path
audience_contract.what_they_should_leave_with: the causal order of the six passes, the contract each boundary hands forward, and where child dossiers hold the depth

upstream.interaction: hands over device functions with multi-dim elementwise chains and reshape noise
enableFlatten, enableAutoVectorizeV2, enableVfMergeLevel, enableHIVMAutoStorageAlign select which stages run

downstream.entity: post-alignment lowering (AFTER_HIVM_STRIDE_ALIGNMENT decompose, InferHIVMDataLayout, buffer-size constantization)
downstream.interaction: consumes the aligned memref IR this chain leaves behind

triggers.interaction: HFusion-level wiring hands to HIVM-level lowering pipelines in one compilation

inputs.name: tensor-level device functions
inputs.form: linalg/hfusion elementwise chains over multi-dim tensors
inputs.description: output of HFusion pre-processing, input to the normalization stages

inputs.name: pipeline options
inputs.description: decide which stages and placements execute

outputs.name: aligned memref IR
outputs.form: padded memref.alloc (e.g. alignment = 64) behind strided logical views, zero leftover marks

outputs.name: VF call graph of chosen granularity
outputs.form: merged (or unmerged) hivm.vector_function callees at tensor or memref level
outputs.description: the structure bufferization and lowering plan over

mechanism.summary: Normalize → vectorize → merge → bufferize → merge → align; two option gates (VF merge level, auto storage align) and one conditional participant (PropagateReshape) sit on an otherwise linear spine.

stages.name: enter with shaped tensor IR
stages.what: entry device function holds multi-dim elementwise chains plus reshape noise

stages.name: normalize shapes
stages.what: PropagateReshape slides reshapes toward producers/outputs; FlattenOps (Tidy, register-based) reduces elementwise bodies to 1-D form bounded by collapse/expand — immediately before AutoVectorizeV2 on the Triton path, earlier in buildHFusionRegBasePipeline otherwise
stages.where: HFusionRegbasePipelines.cpp:567-592 (buildHFusionRegBasePipeline pre-flatten block) and :414-423 (inside hfusionAutoVectorizePipeline, enableSIMDVFFusion branch)

stages.name: vectorize and outline
stages.what: AutoVectorizeV2 tiles/fuses/vectorizes the flat chains; OutlineVectorFunction materializes them as hivm.vector_function callees with call sites

stages.name: merge VF at tensor level (L1, optional)
stages.what: when enableVfMergeLevel==1, MergeVecScope merges adjacent VF callees BEFORE bufferization so the bufferization world sees fewer, larger VFs

stages.name: switch representation: tensor → memref
stages.what: TensorCopyInsertion + OneShotBufferize produce memref IR; this is the largest representation boundary of the chain and the seam between the two merge placements

stages.name: merge VF at memref level (L2, optional)
stages.what: when enableVfMergeLevel==2 (mutually exclusive with L1), MergeVecScope merges after bufferization where concrete memref aliasing is available

stages.name: mark alignment intent
stages.what: PreMarkStrideAlign (regbase protections) + MarkStrideAlign annotate UB memref operands of hivm ops with storage_align marks at hardware alignment units

stages.name: realize alignment
stages.what: FoldAllocReshape first; then EnableStrideAlign unions the marks' demands and re-allocates buffers padded behind strided logical views (no marks → cheap no-op)

stages.name: hand to lowering
stages.what: aligned memref IR with zero leftover marks is consumed by AFTER_HIVM_STRIDE_ALIGNMENT decompose, InferHIVMDataLayout, and buffer-size constantization

implementation_view.description: HFusionRegbasePipelines.cpp owns the HFusion-level stages (normalize, vectorize); HIVMRegbasePipelines.cpp owns bufferizationPipeline and alignStoragePipeline; buildLowerHIVMPipelines sequences the HIVM half

implementation_view.aspect: the two merge placements are if/else on one option
implementation_view.description: enableVfMergeLevel==1 inserts MergeVecScope(mergeLevel=1) before bufferization; ==2 inserts MergeVecScope(mergeLevel=2) after; they never both run

implementation_view.aspect: alignment is split intent vs realization
implementation_view.description: two marking passes sit inside the enableHIVMAutoStorageAlign gate; EnableStrideAlign runs unconditionally and degrades to a no-op without marks

conceptual_view.description: 1-D elementwise bodies let the vectorizer plan over flat last-axis domains without per-dimension case analysis; reshape noise would block the Flattener's collapse-group analysis

conceptual_view.aspect: why VF granularity is a decision point
conceptual_view.description: merging VFs trades call-graph size against merge constraints (dependency, extract kinds, signatures); doing it before vs after bufferization changes what information the merge can use — tensor-level structure vs concrete memref aliasing

conceptual_view.aspect: why alignment is marked then enabled
conceptual_view.description: post-bufferization memref IR is where allocation decisions live; marks express per-op intent, the enabler resolves conflicts (LCM per dim) once at allocations — separating intent from realization keeps both passes simple

provenance.source: STITCHED EXAMPLE — frames from four real bishengir-opt executions of committed tests (flatten, vectorize+outline, mark, enable) plus the child bundle's executed merge-vf runs and a reconstructed bufferization frame; NOT one end-to-end pipeline execution (SYS-EV-016 records this honestly)

canonical_example.initial_state: Entry device function over multi-dim tensors: %a = elemwise over tensor<2x15xf16>-style operands, reshape noise around elementwise chains

execution_trace.description: Frame 1 — normalize (EXECUTED): bishengir-opt --hfusion-flatten-ops on test-drop-unit-extent-dims-and-tidy-flatten.mlir rewrites elementwise chains over collapsed 1-D views (SYS-EV-013); reshape propagation precedes it in the real pipeline (SYS-EV-001)

Frame 2 — vectorize + outline (EXECUTED): bishengir-opt --hfusion-auto-vectorize-v2 --outline-vector-function on auto-vectorize-v2.mlir yields func.func @test_hfusion_indirect_load_outlined_vf_0/1/2 attributes {hivm.vector_function, no_inline} (SYS-EV-012)

Frame 3 — merge at tensor level, L1 (EXECUTED in the MergeVecScope child bundle): --hfusion-merge-vf merge-level=1 on merge-vf-level-1.mlir produces the merged 4-result call (mergevecscope::EV-015); in the real pipeline this placement sits BEFORE bufferization and requires enableVfMergeLevel==1 (SYS-EV-003)
Frame 4 — bufferization (RECONSTRUCTED, not executed): TensorCopyInsertion + OneShotBufferize convert tensor→memref (SYS-EV-003); this is the seam between the two merge placements

Frame 5 — merge at memref level, L2 (child-executed demonstration of the merge output): --hfusion-merge-vf merge-level=2 on merge-vf-level-2.mlir shows the merged memref-level call (mergevecscope::EV-016); its pipeline position is AFTER bufferization, mutually exclusive with L1 (SYS-EV-003) — frames 3 and 5 demonstrate the same pass at its two alternative positions, not a sequence

Frame 6 — mark (EXECUTED): bishengir-opt --hivm-mark-stride-align on hivm-mark-storage-align.mlir emits annotation.mark {hivm.stride_align_dims = array<i32: 0>, hivm.stride_align_value_in_byte = array<i32: 32>} (SYS-EV-010); 32 bytes is that fixture's BL=VL/8 default

Frame 7 — enable (EXECUTED): bishengir-opt -hivm-enable-stride-align on hivm-enable-stride-align-median-kernel.mlir re-allocates with memref.alloc() {alignment = 64} behind strided subviews (SYS-EV-011); 64 is that fixture's unified demand after LCM across marks — mark value (per-op default) and realized alignment (post-unification) come from different fixtures and need not be equal

canonical_example.result: Final state (stitched): aligned memref IR — flattened→vectorized→(merged)→bufferized→marked→realized — ready for post-alignment lowering; each frame's origin is named, the whole is NOT a single execution

decisions.question: Which MergeVecScope placement runs — L1 before bufferization or L2 after?
decisions.condition: hivmPipelineOptions.enableVfMergeLevel: ==1 → L1 (tensor-level, pre-bufferization), ==2 → L2 (memref-level, post-bufferization); mutually exclusive if/else
outcomes: L1: bufferization sees a smaller merged call graph
L2: merge decisions can use concrete memref aliasing
decisions.reason: The option encodes a real design tension: merge early to shrink the bufferization problem, or late to decide with alias information

decisions.question: Is automatic storage alignment active?
decisions.condition: enableHIVMAutoStorageAlign gates the two marking passes (default true); EnableStrideAlign is NOT gated and is a no-op without marks
outcomes: marks absent → chain ends unchanged, cheaply
decisions.reason: Gating intent but not realization keeps the pipeline correct when the gate is off

decisions.question: Does PropagateReshape participate on this target, and where?
decisions.condition: regbase: only the HFusion pre-flatten slots (forRegbased=true); the HIVM-level placements require a NON-reg-based target (anti-regbase conditionals)
outcomes: regbase: reshape cleanup immediately before flattening
membase: additional HIVM-level instances after dialect conversion
decisions.reason: HIVM's brc/reduce same-rank constraint forces reshape insertion only on the non-regbase conversion path — the pass's presence is target-shaped, and the story must show that honestly

decisions.question: Which flatten mode/variant runs at each site, and on which path?
decisions.condition: both regbase placements fix FlattenMode::Tidy + registerBased=true; inside hfusionAutoVectorizePipeline the VFFusion+FlattenOps block runs only when enableSIMDVFFusion ≡ enableTritonKernelCompile; the non-Triton regbase path flattens earlier (buildHFusionRegBasePipeline :569-588, buildHFusionPipelines preFlattenPass/flattenAndFold); a DISTINCT hivm-flatten-ops runs post-bufferization
outcomes: Triton path: flatten sits immediately before AutoVectorizeV2
non-Triton regbase: flatten normalizes earlier, PreVectorizationFusion + canonicalization prepare the vectorizer
HIVM flatten re-flattens memref-level ops after buffer sizing
decisions.reason: Same-named passes at two levels plus a path split is a classic misreading trap; the pipeline wiring proves they are different passes with path-conditional adjacency

contracts.element: reshape-propagated tensor IR (collapse at ends, expand at producers)
1-D elementwise bodies bounded by collapse/expand, external signatures unchanged
smaller merged VF call graph at tensor level
padded aligned allocations behind strided logical views, zero leftover marks

constraints.statement: The two MergeVecScope placements are mutually exclusive (enableVfMergeLevel if/else)
FlattenOps at both regbase sites runs Tidy + register-based; greedy is not the regbase mode
Alignment demands unify per dim (LCM) and conflicting demands resolve loudly (pass failure) or via explicit copy fallback — never silently

invariants.statement: Flattening preserves external function signatures — collapse/expand live inside function bodies only
Reshape propagation preserves element order and element count (legality rejects flip spanning a reassociation group)
VF callee identity (hivm.vector_function attribute) is the stable contract between vectorization and every later stage
Marks are never left dangling: the enabler consumes or errors on them, and the membase certification is stamped separately

boundaries.statement: No single committed test executes the full six-pass chain in one pipeline invocation in this repository — the canonical example is stitched from real per-pass frames, not one end-to-end dump
The legacy AutoVectorize (V1) branch still exists behind enableAutoVectorizeV2=false (maxVectorizeAxes=2); this story covers the V2 path only

The flatten→AutoVectorizeV2 immediate adjacency is Triton-path-specific (enableSIMDVFFusion ≡ enableTritonKernelCompile); on the non-Triton regbase path normalization happens earlier and PreVectorizationFusion + canonicalization precede the vectorizer
PropagateReshape's HIVM-level placements do not run on reg-based targets — on the A5 path the pass exists only in the HFusion pre-flatten slots
The membase-only hivm.storage_aligned certification stamp has no in-repo reader at this HEAD

placement.why_here: The chain is wired across two pipeline files: HFusionRegbasePipelines.cpp for the tensor-level stages and HIVMRegbasePipelines.cpp for bufferization and alignment — the wiring itself is the evidence backbone of this story
placement.why_not_earlier: Vectorization needs normalized 1-D forms; merging and alignment need VF callees and memref IR to exist
placement.why_not_later: Alignment must complete before decompose/layout/buffer-size constantization consume the layout

key_takeaways: 先整形再向量化:1-D elementwise 形态是 AutoVectorizeV2 的输入契约
VF 粒度是一个可调决策:L1/L2 双位置围绕 bufferization,互斥由一个选项控制
对齐意图与对齐实现分离:mark 表达意图,enable 统一需求并落为对齐分配
tensor→memref 是全链最大的表示边界,也是两次 VF merge 的分界
端到端例子是按 pass 拼接的真实帧,不是一次完整执行
